note: Latin-letter stretch 06:00-11:55 (his lines in Arabizi). The 24:10 turn holds three separate pieces: wrong verb بأسب=ba3asseb (D10), preposition منهم/لهم (D11), past tense (A11). 12:15 kaan prompt ('Where؟' = 'Were?') added as its own B6 row; D8 is the adjective-gender row and D20 its duplicate. No agreed row challenged.

row.medi_said: So الواجب عندو تلات سو-- أسول-- أو-- Hold on. أسئلة.
row.amal_said: صح. فيو ثلاث أسئلة. ... فيو، in it. ... It doesn't have. There's in it.
row.why: A thing containing something takes fi (fiho), not 3ind (has); Amal: 'It doesn't have. There's in it.' and he took it ('instead of عندي، فيو').

rulings.why: Both readers saw it; the fix is the small word fi vs 3ind (containment), a preposition choice, so grammar D1; Amal's 'It doesn't have' is an explicit no.

row.amal_said: Mm-mm. Happy with me. ... Happy from, from something I did. ... so minni. ... I heard my.
row.why: inbasat takes min (sheet: 'i feel happy / pleased because of something | Ana banbaset min'); Amal 'Mm-mm', gave minni, and 'I heard my' - he admits 'I did say mayi'.
row.english: You would be happy with me.

rulings.why: Real: Amal said Mm-mm, supplied minni, and he confirmed he said ma3i.

row.medi_said: enno ana barif akhtar arabi min hom.
row.amal_said: إشتى أنا بعرف عربي أكتر منهم.
row.why: 'More' as amount follows the noun (ba3ref 3arabi aktar minhom); Amal recast his whole line with the order swapped and he said Yeah.
row.english: I know Arabic more than them.

rulings.why: Her line is a full recast that changes only the place of aktar.

row.why: He means the cousins (they) and says huwe (he), also at 06:42 'hu-huwe bifhamu'; Amal prompted هم and he said هم at 07:38.

rulings.why: Amal supplied the pronoun and he repeated it at once.

row.medi_said: bifikru el lugha muhim ilhom. Language is gonna be important, yeah.
row.amal_said: ممتاز. So it's going to be.
row.why: He meant 'is going to be important' but gave no future; Amal said 'So it's going to be' and he added rah fikun.
row.english: They think the language is going to be important for them.

rulings.why: Amal's English rephrase is a voiced prompt (PG-22); he then added ra7.

row.medi_said: Oh, it's feminine. Rah fikun muhema ilhom.
row.why: Subject el-lugha is feminine, so ra7 tkoon, not ykoon; he fixed only the adjective and Amal moved on to 'the word for future' (Latin transcript may blur y/t).
row.english: The language is going to be important for them.

rulings.why: Real by the rule (lugha is feminine) but Amal let it pass; low because the Latin transcript may blur fikun/tkun.

row.medi_said: il modara. No, modara is present. ... moraja.
row.amal_said: بس مضارع is only a gram-- it's a grammar term. ... مـ-مس... مستقبل.
row.why: Asked for 'future' he tried مضارع and مراجعة (wrong words); Amal said مضارع is only a grammar term, prompted مـ-مس... and gave مستقبل (sheet: 'future | Musta2bal').

rulings.why: He attempted wrong words (not a plain didn't-know) and the word is on her sheet, so tier 1 not tier 0.

row.medi_said: كان حلووات كتير. كانوا حلوات كتير.
row.amal_said: Are they all كلهم بنات؟ ... لأ، عاد صغار بس حلوين قول حلوات.
row.why: The kids were mixed (he says there was a boy), so the plural adjective is masculine حلوين; Amal asked if they were all girls and he switched to حلوين, she said Mm-hmm.

rulings.why: The adjective-gender row is the one both readers share (r2's A8 version is D20); the 'Where؟' = 'Were?' kaan prompt at 12:15 is written separately in added.

row.why: طلبوني means 'they asked for me'; asking someone takes talab min (he settles on طلبوا مني and Amal accepts it, fixing only the next verb); her طلبوه recast was 'they requested it'.
row.english: Her whole family asked me (to bring it).

rulings.why: Both readers saw the slip on طلبوني; the transcript ends on طلبوا مني, which Amal accepted, so D2 with D4 second.

row.medi_said: Okay. أنا بأسب منهم. ... أنا بأسب لهم
row.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. ... Mm-mm. And about it was I get angry.
row.why: He said ba3asseb (engine بأسب) = 'I get angry' (sheet: 'i get angry | Ana ba3asseb') for 'upset'; Amal said his word was 'I get angry' and he moved to dayi2t (sheet: 'i feel upset about / for someone | Ana batDaaya2 3ala').

rulings.why: This D-row is the wrong-verb slip (Amal's 'that was I get angry'); the preposition slip in the same turn is D11, the past tense is A11.

row.medi_said: أنا بأسب منهم. ... أنا بأسب لهم ... is it ala? Alayhom.
row.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. ... Saħħ.
row.why: Upset for someone takes 3ala (sheet: 'Ana batDaaya2 3ala'); Amal said Mm-mm after منهم and لهم, then Saħħ to ala/alayhom.

rulings.why: Separate piece from D10 (preposition, not the verb); Amal's Mm-mm came before he found ala, so it is not a self-fix.

row.medi_said: Okay, so الـ أول أكل-- الـ أول أكلين؟ No.
row.amal_said: إيش يعني أكلين؟ ... What do you say الأول؟
row.why: awal + noun = first; el- goes on the noun, never before awal; Amal questioned his words ('What do you say الأول؟') and he settled on أول الفيلم.

rulings.why: Kept low: Amal's 'What do you say الأول؟' points at the el- before awal, but he was already restarting with أول الفيلم.

row.medi_said: منيح بس ما حبيت الـ آخرو.
row.amal_said: No ال. Why? ... Why no ال؟
row.why: A word with a pronoun ending is already definite and takes no el-; Amal 'No ال. Why?' and he answered 'cause it's conjugated'.
row.english: It was good but I didn't like the end of it.

rulings.why: Both readers agree; the rule here is about a pronoun ending (A4), with idafa A2 as second.

row.medi_said: أنا قرأت الأخبار. ... I think I said قريت.
row.amal_said: قرأت. ... قرأت. ... It's not. No, no. قرأت.
row.why: Engine wrote قرأت, but he says he said قريت and Amal repeated قرأت three times and said 'No, no'; past form of the verb, may be a hamza sound slip (S4).

rulings.why: Amal voiced the fix three times and he asked 'What did I say?'; low because قريت vs قرأت may be sound-level only.

row.amal_said: الحفلة؟ [تضحك] I wish I would be a حفلة.
row.why: He said حفلة (party) for حرب (war); Amal echoed الحفلة؟ with a laugh and he fixed it to الحرب.

rulings.why: Her laughing echo proves he said حفلة; a different word, tier 1.

row.medi_said: إشي المفضل عندي. Or المفضل إشي عندي.
row.amal_said: Where do you put the Ls? ... Where is the other L? You have another L. Where do you put it?
row.why: With el-mufaddal the noun takes el- too; Amal asked twice for 'the other L' and then said صح (the engine likely dropped his el- on the later line).
row.english: My favorite thing is when I look at nature.

rulings.why: Amal prompted twice for the missing el-; real slip.
Self-fix / restart (S5): Amal's 'وأنا؟' is no tense prompt, and he moved from بحكي to حكيت on his own.

row.medi_said: Uh, their ahel hom, uh, yehku inglisi ma hom.

row.english: Their parents speak English with them.
